mainTopic: Why פסוקים are needed alongside the הלכה about a חטאת and an אשם's offspring and תמורה; רב הונא's rule; and the משנה's dispute about whether a שלמים's offspring is offered
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question from the previous עמוד: why does the ברייתא need a פסוק to exclude the offspring and תמורה of a חטאת and an אשם from the מזבח, when a הלכה already says a חטאת is left to die and an אשם is left to graze? After two answers fall away, the גמרא concludes that the פסוק adds an עשה for anyone who offers such an animal anyway. For רבי עקיבא's source, 'הוא', the גמרא says it teaches רב הונא's rule: an אשם that was sent to graze and then slaughtered without a stated purpose is a valid עולה, but not before it was sent to graze. Next the גמרא explains why the two ברייתות learn the offspring of a שלמים from different פסוקים: they disagree about whether to learn from the word 'אם'. Then a new משנה brings a dispute: רבי אליעזר says a שלמים's offspring is not offered, and the חכמים say it is. רבי שמעון limits the dispute to the direct offspring, and רבי יהושע and רבי פפייס testify that the offspring was offered. The גמרא first tries a פסוק as רבי אליעזר's source, rejects it, and explains his rule as a גזירה so people won't raise herds from קרבנות. Finally, רבה and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree about רבי שמעון's words. רבה says everyone agrees the grand-offspring are offered, and רבי יהושע בן לוי says everyone agrees they are not.

steps.title: The guilt offering side of the question: a tradition already sends it to graze
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge. If the פסוק is about the תמורה of an אשם, we already have a tradition that such an animal is left to graze, so the פסוק teaches nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the verse is talking about a guilt offering, we already know by tradition that it goes out to graze, since whenever a sin offering is left to die, in the matching case of a guilt offering the animal grazes.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the question the גמרא started just before this. It shows that the אשם case also needs no פסוק, because a tradition already covers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said that if the פסוק is about a חטאת, the הלכה already says it is left to die. Now it adds that if the פסוק is about an אשם, the הלכה already says it grazes. With both cases covered, the פסוק seems to have no job.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned it by tradition, meaning a הלכה passed down orally, not taken from a פסוק
Grazing. The animal is left in the pasture until it gets a blemish, and then it is redeemed.
A sin offering that is left to die, such as one whose owner already got atonement with a different animal
Guilt offering

phrases.english: If it is of a guilt offering —
phrases.notes: He means: if the פסוק is excluding the substitute of an אשם.

phrases.english: it is learned by tradition that it goes to grazing,
for whatever case of a sin offering dies,
in a guilt offering, it grazes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּאָשָׁם גְּמִירִי לַהּ דְּלִרְעִיָּיה אָזְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question from the previous section (the חטאת side was already raised).
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's need for a פסוק to exclude the ולדות and תמורות of חטאת and אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both the חטאת and the אשם outcomes are already known from a הלכה, so the פסוק is unnecessary.

steps.title: First answer: the tradition is about death, the verse is about offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא really is about a חטאת. The הלכה teaches that the animal is left to die, and the פסוק teaches that it may not be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the verse is about a sin offering. The tradition teaches that it is left to die, and the verse comes to exclude it from being offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to give the פסוק its own job. Each source teaches something different: one teaches death, the other teaches no offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the הלכה only tells us what to do with the animal (let it die). The פסוק adds a separate rule that it may not be brought on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Really. This word signals the גמרא is keeping its first understanding and defending it.
Death, here meaning letting the animal die
Offering the animal on the מזבח

phrases.english: Actually, it is about a sin offering,
and the tradition was learned for death,
and the verse is to exclude it from offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם בְּחַטָּאת וְהִילְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ לְמִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by splitting the jobs of the הלכה and the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Division of roles between two sources
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק and the הלכה teach the same thing, so the פסוק is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלכה teaches death and the פסוק teaches the ban on offering.

steps.title: Challenge: if it must die, obviously it is not offered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this answer. If an animal must be left to die, it automatically cannot be offered, so the פסוק still adds nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this depends on that! Since it goes to its death, it obviously is not offered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave and shows the two rules are really one rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Letting the animal die and not offering it are not two separate laws. Once it must die, a ban on offering comes along with it automatically, so the פסוק still has no job.

keyTerms.meaning: This depends on that; the two ideas are tied together
Automatically, by itself

phrases.english: But this depends on that,
phrases.notes: 'This' is not offering it, and 'that' is letting it die.

phrases.english: since it goes to death —
automatically it is not offered!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the answer in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פסוק teaches a separate ban on offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not offering follows automatically from being left to die, so nothing new is learned.

steps.title: Second answer: the tradition covers the sin offering, the verse covers the guilt offering's substitute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries again. The הלכה is only about a חטאת, and the פסוק is needed to exclude the תמורה of an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the tradition is about a sin offering, and the verse comes to exclude the substitute of a guilt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. It moves the פסוק's job over to the אשם case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer, the oral tradition only talks about a חטאת. The פסוק is what teaches that the תמורה of an אשם is not offered.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute animal. Someone tried to swap a non-sacred animal for a sacred one, and both become sacred.
The tradition, a law passed down orally

phrases.english: Rather, the tradition is for a sin offering,
and the verse is to exclude the substitute of a guilt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הִלְכְתָא לְחַטָּאת וְקָרָא לְמַעוֹטֵי תְּמוּרַת אָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 2 with a new division of roles.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases between the הלכה and the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק and the הלכה both deal with the same חטאת case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלכה covers the חטאת and the פסוק covers the תמורה of the אשם.

steps.title: Challenge: the guilt offering is also covered by the tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second answer. The same tradition already says that an אשם in a matching case grazes, so the פסוק is again unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this too was learned by tradition, as they say: whatever case of a sin offering dies, in a guilt offering it grazes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the tradition itself includes the אשם, so the second answer also fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tradition is one rule with two parts: the חטאת dies and the אשם grazes. Since the אשם is part of it, the פסוק still is not needed for the אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: This too
It grazes

phrases.english: This too was learned by tradition,
as they say: whatever case of a sin offering dies,
in a guilt offering, it grazes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פסוק is needed for the תמורה of an אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same tradition already covers the אשם case.

steps.title: Final answer: the verse adds a positive commandment for one who offered it anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the פסוק is needed for something else. If someone went ahead and offered such an animal, he has also broken an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse is needed to teach that if one transgressed and offered it, he stands in violation of a positive commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a real job for the פסוק. It does not decide what happens to the animal; it adds a sin for whoever offers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה tells us what to do with these animals. The פסוק says that only the offspring and substitutes of עולה and שלמים are offered, which implies the others may not be. A ban that comes from a positive command counts as an עשה, so offering them breaks an עשה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for
He transgressed and offered it
He stands in violation of a positive commandment

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה tells us what happens to the animal (a חטאת dies, an אשם grazes). The פסוק adds that whoever offers one of these animals anyway breaks an עשה.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק is not teaching that these animals cannot be offered; we already knew that. It teaches that offering one is an extra sin, an עשה.

phrases.english: Rather, the verse is needed for him,
that if he transgressed and offered it —
he stands in violation of a positive commandment.
phrases.notes: The פסוק says only some animals are offered, so offering the others goes against what that positive command implies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא קְרָא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ דְּאִי עָבַר וּמַקְרֵיב קָאֵי בַּעֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both splitting answers fail, gives the פסוק a separate legal job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the פסוק a new legal job (an added עשה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק must be teaching the fate of the animal, which the הלכה already teaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק adds an עשה for someone who offers such an animal anyway.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a פסוק can be needed even when a הלכה gives the same practical result, because the פסוק adds a sin for doing it anyway.

steps.title: Quoting רבי עקיבא: the guilt offering is offered but not its substitute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now quotes רבי עקיבא's opinion from the ברייתא. The extra word is not needed, because the פסוק about the אשם itself teaches that the אשם is offered and its תמורה is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: it is not needed, and so on. It is offered, but its substitute is not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new discussion by quoting the other opinion in the ברייתא, רבי עקיבא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learns the rule from the word 'הוא' ('it') in the פסוק about the אשם: only the אשם itself is offered. This gives a different source than רבי ישמעאל's for excluding the תמורה of an אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed
And so on; the rest of the quote is left out
It is offered; 'הוּא' (it) limits the rule to the אשם itself

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: it is not needed, etc.
phrases.notes: He means the word 'רק' (only) is not needed to exclude these animals.

phrases.english: It is offered, but its substitute is not offered.
phrases.notes: From the פסוק 'אָשָׁם הוּא' (ויקרא 5:19).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי ישמעאל's opinion to רבי עקיבא's opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the אשם itself is offered, not its תמורה, learned from 'הוּא'.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי עקיבא: why a verse if there is a tradition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא needs a פסוק at all, since the הלכה already says the תמורה of an אשם grazes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a verse? Wasn't this learned by tradition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא aims the same kind of question it asked about רבי ישמעאל at רבי עקיבא. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tradition that an אשם grazes whenever a חטאת would die already teaches that the תמורה of an אשם is not offered. So רבי עקיבא's source from 'הוּא' seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need a verse? A standard challenge that a source seems unnecessary

phrases.english: Why do I need a verse,
but it was learned by tradition!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי קְרָא וְהָא הִילְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's source just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's use of 'הוּא' to exclude the תמורה of an אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הלכה that an אשם grazes already teaches this, so the פסוק is unnecessary.

steps.title: The פסוק is needed for רב הונא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the פסוק is not needed for the תמורה of an אשם. Instead it teaches רב הונא's rule: an אשם sent to graze and then slaughtered without a stated purpose is valid as an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. So why do I need the פסוק? It is needed for רב הונא's rule. רב הונא said: an אשם that was sent off to graze, and someone slaughtered it without saying what it was for, is valid as an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the question was right: the הלכה already tells us the תמורה of an אשם grazes. So it gives the פסוק a new job, which is to teach רב הונא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם that can no longer be brought as an אשם is 'sent to graze' until it gets a blemish, and then its money goes to buy עולות. רב הונא says that if someone slaughtered it before that without naming a purpose, it still works as an עולה. The פסוק in רבי עקיבא's ברייתא is now the source for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so. The גמרא agrees with the question.
Sent off to graze. The animal is set aside until it gets a blemish, because it cannot be offered as it is.
Without stating a purpose; unspecified
Valid as an עולה

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא does not say the animal stops being in the category of an אשם in general. He is talking about the unusual result for an אשם that was already sent to graze: once that has happened, slaughtering it without a stated purpose counts as an עולה.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
phrases.notes: He means: you are right, the פסוק is not needed to teach about the תמורה of an אשם.

phrases.english: but then why do I need the verse?
It is needed for the rule of רב הונא,
as רב הונא said:
A guilt offering that was sent off to graze
and he slaughtered it without stating a purpose —
it is valid as a burnt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא קְרָא לְמָה לִי? מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by agreeing with its point and giving the פסוק a different job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the challenge and reassigns the פסוק to a different הלכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק teaches that the תמורה of an אשם is not offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches רב הונא's rule about an אשם that was sent to graze.

steps.title: Only if it was sent to graze, because 'הוא' means it stays as it is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads רב הונא carefully: only an אשם already sent to graze is valid as an עולה. Before that it is not, because the פסוק says 'הוא', meaning it stays an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was sent to graze, yes, it is valid. If it was not sent to graze, no, it is not. What is the reason? The פסוק says 'הוא', meaning it stays in its present state.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא learns something from the exact wording of רב הונא and then gives the reason. Before the animal is sent to graze, it cannot become an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows exactly what the פסוק adds. The word 'הוא' keeps the animal locked as an אשם as long as it has not been sent to graze. Once it is sent to graze, that lock is gone, and slaughtering it without a stated purpose makes it a valid עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
'It is.' This word in the פסוק about the אשם shows the animal stays what it is.
It shall stay in its present state

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's rule: an אשם sent to graze and slaughtered without a stated purpose is a valid עולה. If it was not yet sent to graze, it is not valid, because 'הוא' keeps it an אשם.

phrases.english: If it was sent to graze — yes, it is valid,
if it was not sent to graze — no, it is not.
What is the reason?
The verse says 'It is' — meaning it shall stay as it is.
phrases.notes: This is the word 'הוא' in the פסוק that calls the animal 'אשם הוא', 'it is a guilt offering.'

steps.triggerLanguage: נִיתַּק — אִין, לֹא נִיתַּק — לָא. מַאי טַעְמָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads רב הונא's rule precisely and gives the reason, based on a word in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם not yet sent to graze is not valid as an עולה, because 'הוא' means it stays an אשם.

steps.title: Why not learn from 'זכר' and 'נקבה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the second ברייתא, which learns the offspring of a שלמים from other פסוקים. It asks why that תנא does not just learn it from 'זכר' and 'נקבה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to this תנא who learns it from these פסוקים, let him learn it from 'male' and 'female'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic, going back to the two ברייתות from the previous עמוד about the offspring of a שלמים. It challenges the תנא who used a different source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא learned that the offspring of a שלמים is a שלמים from 'אם זכר אם נקבה' in the פסוק about שלמים. The second ברייתא learned it from 'תשא ובאת' and the פסוק about the flesh and the blood. The question is why the second תנא needs those פסוקים when 'זכר' and 'נקבה' are right there.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period, here the author of the second ברייתא
Learns out; derives
Let me derive it from. This suggests a more obvious source.
Male and female, words from the פסוק about שלמים (ויקרא 3:1)

phrases.english: And according to this tanna
phrases.notes: This is the second ברייתא from the previous עמוד, which learned the offspring of a שלמים from 'תשא ובאת'.

phrases.english: who derives it from these verses,
let him derive it from 'male' and 'female'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:1

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְהַאי תַּנָּא דְּקָא יָלֵיף מֵהָנֵי קְרָאֵי, תִּיפּוֹק לִי מִ״זָּכָר״ וּ״נְקֵבָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אשם discussion and goes back to the earlier ברייתות about the offspring of a שלמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second ברייתא's choice of source for the offspring of a שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler source, 'זכר' and 'נקבה', is available, so why use other פסוקים?

steps.title: 'זכר' and 'נקבה' teach about blemished animals
steps.stepSummary: The second תנא needs 'זכר' and 'נקבה' for a different law: the offspring and the תמורה of blemished animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that פסוק for the offspring of blemished animals and for the תמורה of blemished animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second תנא already uses 'זכר' and 'נקבה' for something else, so he needs other פסוקים for the offspring of a regular שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק can teach only one thing. For this תנא, 'זכר' and 'נקבה' teach that the offspring and the תמורה of a blemished קדשים animal also have holiness. So the law about the offspring of an unblemished שלמים has to come from 'תשא ובאת'.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring of an animal
Animals with a blemish
An animal swapped in for a holy animal, which becomes holy too

phrases.english: He needs that verse
for the offspring of blemished animals,
and for the substitute of blemished animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לִוְלַד בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by showing that 'זכר' and 'נקבה' are already used for another law.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק is needed for a different derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זכר' and 'נקבה' are free to teach about the offspring of a שלמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: For this תנא, 'זכר' and 'נקבה' teach about the offspring and the תמורה of blemished animals.

steps.title: Why not learn everything from this one פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the second תנא does not learn all the laws from the פסוק 'אם זכר אם נקבה', the way the first תנא did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him learn all of them from this פסוק!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further: the first תנא got all the laws from this one פסוק, so why can't the second תנא do the same?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first תנא learned the offspring and the תמורה of both unblemished and blemished animals from the extra words in 'אם זכר אם נקבה'. If that works, the second תנא would not need 'תשא ובאת' at all.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them, meaning all the laws together

phrases.english: But let him derive all of them
from this verse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 12 by suggesting that one פסוק could teach everything.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second תנא's need for a separate source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first תנא learned everything from 'אם זכר אם נקבה', so the second could do the same.

steps.title: The second תנא does not learn from the word 'אם'
steps.stepSummary: The second תנא does not treat the word 'אם' as extra, so he cannot learn more laws from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not learn anything from the word 'if'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two תנאים disagree about the word 'אם'. The second תנא does not learn anything from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first תנא got the extra laws from the repeated word 'אם'. The second תנא sees 'אם' as a normal word, not an extra one, so the פסוק only gives him 'זכר' and 'נקבה'. That is why he needs 'תשא ובאת' for the offspring of a regular שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If', a word in the פסוק 'אם זכר אם נקבה'
It does not mean anything to him, so he does not learn from it

steps.whatToRemember: The two ברייתות disagree because one תנא learns from the word 'אם' and the other does not. So the second תנא uses 'זכר' and 'נקבה' for blemished animals and 'תשא ובאת' for the offspring of a שלמים.

phrases.english: He does not derive anything from 'if'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by showing the two תנאים disagree about learning from 'אם'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disagreement about how to read a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second תנא could learn every law from 'אם זכר אם נקבה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second תנא does not learn from 'אם', so the פסוק cannot teach him all the laws.

steps.title: What does the first תנא do with 'You shall take and go'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the opposite question: the first תנא learns everything from 'זכר' and 'נקבה', so what does he use the פסוק 'תשא ובאת' for?
steps.simpleTranslation: And this תנא learns it from 'male' and 'if female.' So what does he do with the words 'You shall take and go'?
steps.whatsHappening: Earlier the גמרא asked why the second תנא does not use 'זכר ונקבה'. Now it asks the reverse: what does the first תנא do with the פסוק the second תנא used?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that no words in the תורה are wasted. If the first תנא gets the law of a שלמים's offspring from 'אם זכר אם נקבה', then 'תשא ובאת' seems to have no job. The גמרא wants to know what it teaches for him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall take and go', the פסוק about bringing קדשים to the בית המקדש
Male
Female

phrases.english: And according to this תנא, who derives it
phrases.notes: This is the תנא of the first ברייתא, who learned all the laws from 'אם זכר אם נקבה'.

phrases.english: from 'male' and 'if female,'
what does he do with 'you shall take and go'?
phrases.notes: דברים 12:26

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְהַאי תַּנָּא דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִזָּכָר אִם נְקֵבָה תִּשָּׂא וּבָאתָ מָה עָבֵיד לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question from Steps 11 and 13 the other way, now aimed at the first תנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first תנא's derivation from 'זכר' and 'נקבה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'זכר ונקבה' teaches the law, the פסוק 'תשא ובאת' seems to have nothing left to teach for him.

steps.title: Bring the animals even from the pasture, or from threshing
steps.stepSummary: The first תנא uses 'תשא ובאת' to teach that you must bring your קרבנות at the רגל, even if you have to pull the animals out of the pasture. Another version says even out of threshing work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even from their grazing. Another version: even from their threshing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for the first תנא, 'תשא ובאת' teaches a different lesson: do not put off bringing your קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'You shall take' means you must actively bring the animal at the coming רגל, even when that is inconvenient, like when it is out grazing. The second version gives a stronger case: even when the animal is busy threshing and you need it for work. Either way, the פסוק has its own job, so the question is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Pasture, a place where animals graze
Threshing sledge, threshing work
Another version of the answer

phrases.english: Even from their grazing.
phrases.notes: He means you must bring them to ירושלים at the רגל even if you have to take them off the pasture.

phrases.english: Another version: from their threshing.
phrases.notes: Even if the animal is in the middle of threshing work, don't wait. Bring it now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15 by giving 'תשא ובאת' its own separate lesson.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the פסוק to a different law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'תשא ובאת' would be left with no use for the first תנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that you must not delay bringing קרבנות, even when you have to take the animal from grazing or from threshing.
steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים use every פסוק. They only disagree about which פסוק teaches which law.

steps.title: The משנה: is a שלמים's offspring offered?
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: רבי אליעזר says the offspring of a שלמים is not offered as a שלמים, and the חכמים say it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי אליעזר says the offspring of a peace offering is not offered as a peace offering. The חכמים say it is offered.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It shows that the status of a שלמים's offspring is actually a disagreement between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה said plainly that the offspring of a שלמים is like a שלמים. Here we learn that רבי אליעזר disagrees: in his view the offspring is not brought on the מזבח. The חכמים hold that it is offered as a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Offspring of an animal
Peace offering
It is offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: Mishnah
Rabbi Eliezer says:
The offspring of a peace offering is not offered as a peace offering,
and the Rabbis say: it is offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר וְלַד שְׁלָמִים לֹא יִקְרַב שְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא's discussion of the two ברייתות ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: a שלמים's offspring is not offered. חכמים: it is offered as a שלמים.

steps.title: רבי שמעון narrows the dispute to the first offspring
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says רבי אליעזר and the חכמים do not argue about the grand-offspring of a שלמים, or of its תמורה. Their dispute is only about the direct offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: They did not argue about the offspring of the offspring of a שלמים, or the offspring of the offspring of a תמורה, whether it is offered. What did they argue about? The offspring itself. רבי אליעזר says it is not offered, and the חכמים say it is.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון clarifies exactly where רבי אליעזר and the חכמים disagree. It is only about the first generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון limits the argument to the direct offspring of the שלמים. For the second generation, both sides agree. Which way they agree, offered or not offered, is the question the גמרא raises in step 25.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not disagree
The offspring of the offspring, the second generation
An animal swapped for a קרבן, which becomes holy too

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: They did not disagree
about the offspring of the offspring of a peace offering,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל וְלַד וְלַד תְּמוּרָה שֶׁלֹּא יִקְרַב.
phrases.english: or about the offspring of the offspring of a substitute, that it is not offered.
phrases.notes: Agree it's NOT offered, or agree it IS offered? The גמרא asks exactly this in step 25.

phrases.english: About what did they disagree? About the offspring itself.
Rabbi Eliezer says: it is not offered,
and the Rabbis say: it is offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the dispute stated in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no dispute about the second generation. The dispute is only about the direct offspring.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume you already know which way the 'no dispute' goes for the grand-offspring. The גמרא asks this in step 25, and רבה and רבי יהושע בן לוי answer it in opposite ways.

steps.title: Testimony that the offspring was offered
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע and רבי פפייס testify that a שלמים's offspring is offered as a שלמים. רבי פפייס tells of his own family's cow and her calf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע and רבי פפייס testified that the offspring of a שלמים is offered as a שלמים. רבי פפייס said: I testify that we had a cow that was a שלמים. We ate it on פסח, and we ate its offspring as a שלמים on the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: Two sages bring testimony that backs up the חכמים: the offspring of a שלמים really is offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a real event is used as proof. רבי פפייס's family offered the mother cow as a שלמים on פסח, and later offered her calf as a שלמים on the חג. That shows in practice that the offspring is treated as a שלמים, which matches the view of the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Testified, gave formal testimony about a law
Peace-offering sacrifices
'The Festival', usually סוכות

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Pappeyas testified
about the offspring of a peace offering, that it is offered as a peace offering.
Rabbi Pappeyas said: I testify

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיְתָה לָנוּ פָּרָה שֶׁל זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים,
phrases.english: that we had a cow that was a peace offering,
and we ate it on Pesach,
and we ate its offspring as a peace offering on the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the חכמים's side of the dispute in Steps 17 and 18.
steps.raayaObject: The view of the חכמים that a שלמים's offspring is offered
steps.raayaSupportSource: Testimony of רבי יהושע and רבי פפייס, including a real case from רבי פפייס's family
steps.whatToRemember: The testimony backs the חכמים: the direct offspring of a שלמים is offered as a שלמים.

steps.title: A verse-based reason for רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי quotes רבי יוחנן: רבי אליעזר learns from 'ואם זבח שלמים' that only the mother is offered, not the offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What is רבי אליעזר's reason? The פסוק says 'And if (ואם) his offering is a שלמים.' Read it as 'And a mother (ואם)': the mother is offered, but not the offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of רבי אליעזר's view in the משנה, and רבי יוחנן answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ואם' (and if) is spelled the same as 'ואם' (and a mother). רבי יוחנן reads it as 'mother', so the פסוק limits the שלמים to the mother animal and excludes its offspring.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
A peace-offering sacrifice
The mother, but not the offspring

steps.confusionAlert: The word in the פסוק really means 'and if'. רבי יוחנן is not changing the פסוק. He is using the fact that it can also be read as 'and a mother' to teach a הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Ami said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?
phrases.notes: This is his view in the משנה that the offspring of a שלמים is not brought as a שלמים.

phrases.english: The verse says
"And if his offering is a peace-offering sacrifice to ה׳"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:1

phrases.english: "And a mother" — but not the offspring.
phrases.notes: He reads וְאִם, 'and if', as וְאֵם, 'and a mother', since the letters are the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה from step 17 by giving רבי אליעזר's source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר's reason is the פסוק 'ואם זבח שלמים', read as 'mother and not offspring'.

steps.title: The same reading would apply to תודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא asks: by that logic, 'אם על תודה' should also mean only the mother is a תודה, not its offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said to רבי אמי: But if so, the פסוק about תודה says 'If (אם) he offers it for a thanksgiving.' Would that also mean the mother and not the offspring?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא attacks the reading from step 20 by applying it to a similar פסוק about the תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'אם' can be read as 'mother' by שלמים, it should also be read that way by תודה. That would mean the offspring of a תודה is not brought as a תודה. The next step will show why that is a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (a challenge that pushes your logic further)
Thanksgiving offering

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said to Rabbi Ami:
But if so,
"If he offers it for a thanksgiving"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:12

phrases.english: would it also mean the mother and not the offspring?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of 'ואם' given in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading of 'ואם' as 'mother, not offspring'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reading would apply to 'אם על תודה', which would wrongly exclude the offspring of a תודה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a תודה's offspring is brought
steps.stepSummary: You can't say the offspring of a תודה is not brought, because a ברייתא learns from 'אם על תודה' that the offspring, תמורה, and replacement are all brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that is true, isn't it taught in a ברייתא: Its offspring, its substitute, and its replacement, from where do we know they are brought? The פסוק says 'If for a thanksgiving', meaning in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the escape route: you can't just accept that the offspring of a תודה is not brought, because a ברייתא says it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the very same word 'אם' in the תודה פסוק to include the offspring, not to exclude it. So the word 'אם' cannot be the source for excluding offspring, and רבי יוחנן's reason from step 20 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say, yes, that is so
An animal swapped for a קרבן, which also becomes holy
A replacement animal set aside for a lost קרבן
In any case

phrases.english: And if you say, yes, that is so,
but isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Its offspring, its substitute, and its replacement — from where do we know they are brought?
phrases.notes: 'Replacement' is an animal set aside after the first תודה was lost, when the first one is later found.

phrases.english: The verse says, "If for a thanksgiving"
meaning in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 21 by blocking the answer 'yes, a תודה's offspring is also not brought'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible answer that רבי אליעזר also excludes a תודה's offspring.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא reads 'אם על תודה' as including the offspring, so 'אם' cannot mean 'mother, not offspring'.

steps.title: The real reason: a rabbinic decree against building herds
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא gives a new reason in רבי יוחנן's name: רבי אליעזר's rule is a גזירה, so people won't raise whole herds from their שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is רבי אליעזר's reason: it is a גזירה, so that a person won't raise whole herds from them.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the verse-based reason failed, the גמרא gives a completely different reason for רבי אליעזר: a rabbinic decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תורה, the offspring could be brought. But the רבנן worried that if offspring could be offered, an owner might hold off bringing his שלמים and breed whole herds to sell as קרבנות. So רבי אליעזר's rule comes from the רבנן, not from the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to prevent a problem
Lest; maybe (worry about what might happen)
Whole herds and herds

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's view that a שלמים's offspring is not brought is a rabbinic גזירה, so people won't breed herds from קרבנות. It is not learned from a פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
This is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer:
it is a decree, lest he raise from them
whole herds and herds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected verse-based reason of step 20 with a new reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the source: a rabbinic decree instead of a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר learned from 'ואם' that only the mother is offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר's rule is a גזירה so people won't raise herds from their קרבנות.

steps.title: Quoting רבי שמעון's line from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, where רבי שמעון says there is no dispute about the grand-offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: They did not disagree, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new discussion by quoting רבי שמעון's words from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line was already taught in step 18. Here it is quoted only as a heading, to open the גמרא's discussion of רבי שמעון's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not disagree
Etc. (short for the rest of the quote)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: They did not disagree, etc.
phrases.notes: This is the line from step 18, about the grand-offspring of a שלמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי אליעזר's reason to the next statement in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces רבי שמעון's statement that there is no dispute about the grand-offspring.

steps.title: Which way did רבי שמעון mean 'no dispute'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי שמעון meant that everyone agrees the grand-offspring are brought, or that everyone agrees they are not brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: How is the משנה worded? Is it 'They do not disagree that they are not brought; rather, they are brought'? Or maybe 'They do not disagree that they are brought; rather, they are not brought'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about how to read רבי שמעון's words in the משנה. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said there is 'no dispute' about the grand-offspring, but he did not say which side everyone agrees on. Option one: even רבי אליעזר agrees they are brought. Option two: even the רבנן agree they are not brought.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open question the Sages asked)
How is it taught? How exactly should the wording be read?
They did not disagree
They are offered on the מזבח
The offspring of the offspring (the grand-offspring)

steps.confusionAlert: 'No dispute' does not tell you the answer. It only tells you both sides agree. The whole question is WHICH side they agree on.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them: How is it taught?
phrases.notes: This is about רבי שמעון's line from the משנה, quoted just before: no dispute about the grand-offspring.

phrases.english: "They did not disagree over whether they are not brought,
rather, they are brought"?
Or perhaps: "They did not disagree over whether they are brought,
rather, they are not brought"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to read the line of רבי שמעון quoted in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the agreement about the grand-offspring is that they are brought or that they are not brought.

steps.title: רבה: everyone agrees the grand-offspring are brought
steps.stepSummary: רבה says everyone agrees the grand-offspring are brought, because רבי אליעזר only argued about the direct offspring. Grand-offspring come up only by rare chance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It makes sense to read 'They do not disagree that they are not brought; rather, they are brought.' Why? רבי אליעזר only argues with the רבנן about the offspring. But the grand-offspring only happens by chance.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question. He says even רבי אליעזר agrees the grand-offspring may be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's rule was a גזירה, so people won't raise herds from their שלמים (step 23). רבה says a grand-offspring is a rare event that happens on its own, not a common pattern. So the גזירה was never needed for it, and it may be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it makes sense
What is the reason?
He only disagrees up to here (his argument is limited to this case)
Just a rare chance; something unusual

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a גזירה usually covers only the common case. A rare case is left with the basic rule.

phrases.english: Rabba said: It stands to reason
"They did not disagree over whether they are not brought; rather, they are brought."
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיג רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer only disagrees
with the Rabbis about the offspring,
but the offspring of the offspring —
that is merely by chance.
phrases.notes: He means it is rare for someone to wait so long that the offspring itself has babies, so there's nothing to prevent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25 with the first option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The grand-offspring are brought by everyone's opinion, since the גזירה does not apply to a rare case.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: everyone agrees the grand-offspring are not brought
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says everyone agrees the grand-offspring are NOT brought. Waiting that long shows the owner wants to raise a herd.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The reading is 'They do not disagree that they are brought; rather, they are not brought.' Why? The רבנן only argue with רבי אליעזר about the offspring. But with the grand-offspring, his actions show what he is thinking: he wants to raise animals from it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives the opposite answer. He says even the רבנן agree the grand-offspring may not be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה looked at the grand-offspring as a rare accident. רבי יהושע בן לוי looks at it as a sign. If the owner waited long enough for a grand-offspring to be born, he clearly meant to raise a herd. That is exactly what the גזירה is meant to stop, so even the רבנן agree.

keyTerms.meaning: From his actions his intention can be seen
To raise (animals, to build up a herd)
The Sages who argue with רבי אליעזר (the majority view)

steps.whatToRemember: רבה: grand-offspring are brought by all, since a long delay is just rare chance. רבי יהושע בן לוי: grand-offspring are not brought by all, since a long delay shows he wants to raise a herd. Both agree there is no dispute. They only disagree about which side everyone agrees on.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
"They did not disagree over whether they are brought; rather, they are not brought."
What is the reason?
The Rabbis only disagree
with Rabbi Eliezer about the offspring,
but the offspring of the offspring —
